headline: An Anthropic executive said open-source AI models carry more risk than closed ones.
score_reason: Pool score kept: on-record view from a senior executive of a leading AI lab, but a short TV remark and from a company that sells closed models.
importance_line: The remark feeds the live argument over whether publicly released model weights make AI safer or more dangerous, which affects open-model developers, governments writing rules and companies choosing between open and closed models, but it is one executive's view, not a finding.
summary: Bloomberg reports that Guillaume Princen, head of international at Anthropic, the maker of the Claude chatbot, told Bloomberg TV at an AI summit in Dublin that "by definition, there's more risk" with open models, adding "We need to be really careful with open-source on safety." Anthropic sells closed models, so the view comes from a company with a commercial stake in the argument.
